title: how commands get their own session id (${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID})
summary: Claude Code substitutes ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID} into a command markdown file's `!`-prefixed bash execution body, giving a slash command its own session id even though the official docs say hook-style stdin fields (session_id, transcript_path) are documented as available to hooks only, not slash commands — this repo has two independent, working proofs of the substitution.

steps.role: second independent proof: passes ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID} to scripts/usage.mjs --session

invariants: Not documented for slash commands by the official Claude Code docs (checked hooks.md) — only confirmed empirically via these two files' working behavior.
A companion gap: there is no equivalent substitution for a command's own transcript_path — it must be derived (cwd-encoding + session id), not read directly.
